sources.entry: Anima - Native macOS companion for Claude Code with per-project ASCII familiars, nim token economy, and cross-session watcher. Built with Tauri v2.

summary.one_liner: Anima is a native macOS client for Claude Code, built with Tauri v2, that runs multiple sessions in one window and adds per-project ASCII companions, a cross-session pattern watcher, and an @nim@ token-reward system.
summary.what_it_does: Anima spawns Claude Code as a subprocess, pipes its stream-json output, and renders messages in its own UI, with a dashboard showing which sessions are working, done, or waiting. A Rust daemon (daemon.rs) polls session activity and tracks tool sequences across all active sessions to flag retry loops and read-heavy spirals. Each project folder gets a generated ASCII familiar with species, rarity, and stats, and it animates while Claude works. Every 1,000 tokens earns 1 @nim@, which can be spent on re-rolls. Companion commentary is produced by a `claude -p` subprocess and shown in a selectable speech bubble that can be pasted back into a session. The app also includes a session history browser (JSONL-backed), optional voice input via a WebSocket bridge, and per-session model and effort overrides.
use_cases: monitor multiple Claude Code sessions at once
detect retry loops in AI coding agent sessions
use a native macOS GUI for Claude Code
voice input for Claude Code via push-to-talk
track token usage with a reward system
how_to_run: git lfs install && git lfs pull
notable: Cross-session Rust daemon that detects retry loops and read-heavy spirals across all active Claude Code sessions
Per-project ASCII companion with deterministic species, rarity, and stats; same project yields the same buddy
@nim@ token economy: 1 nim per 1,000 tokens, spent on companion re-rolls
Companion commentary uses the full Claude model via claude -p, with selectable text for pasting back into sessions
Vanilla JS frontend with no framework or bundler
caveats: Requires macOS 13 or later on Apple Silicon and an authenticated Claude Code CLI
No signed .dmg published; must build from source, and the build is unsigned so Gatekeeper warns on first launch
Voice is optional and the bundled STT sidecar is disabled by default; live voice needs an external WebSocket STT bridge
Alpha software from a solo developer; breaking changes happen
